title: Guess My Number
pitch: Build a game nobody can beat.

words.intro: Build a real game: the computer picks a secret number and gives **higher** or **lower** hints. Then flip it, so the computer guesses *yours*.
words.finished: You built two games, and a guessing trick that never needs more than 7 tries.
words.tinker: Keep tinkering: make it 1 to 1000 (how many tries does the machine need now?), or add a limit of 7 guesses.

milestones.title: Pick a secret
milestones.goal: The computer secretly picks a number from 1 to 100.

steps.instruction: What number do you think the computer will pick? Make your guess, then **Run** it two or three times.
choices: A number from 1 to 10, often different each time
steps.explain: `random.randint(1, 10)` rolls a 10-sided dice: any whole number from 1 to 10, both ends included. Run it again and you'll probably get a different one.
hints: Look at `random.randint(1, 10)`.
`randint` means "random integer": a random whole number between the two numbers.
`random.randint(1, 6)` is like rolling a dice.
It picks a number from 1 to __, and it can change every Run.
A number from 1 to 10, often different each time. Pick that and Run it a few times.

steps.instruction: Make the game harder: change it to pick from **1 to 100**, and delete the `Psst` line so the secret stays secret.
hints: Two changes: the second number in `randint`, and the last line.
`random.randint(low, high)` picks between low and high. A `print` shows things, so the Psst line gives the secret away.
`random.randint(1, 50)` would pick from 1 to 50.
`secret = random.randint(1, ___)`, and remove `print("Psst, it's", secret)`.
Change it to `secret = random.randint(1, 100)` and delete the whole Psst line. Update the message to say 1 to 100 too.

milestones.title: Ask for a guess
milestones.goal: The player types a guess and gets a hint.

steps.instruction: New code with `input()`. What happens when you press Run?
choices: It waits for you to type a guess in the output panel
steps.explain: `input("Your guess: ")` shows the question and **waits** for you to type and press Enter. `int(...)` turns what you typed into a number, so Python can compare it with the secret.

check.description: Your game asked a question and listened!

hints: Look at the line with `input(...)`.
`input()` pauses the program until someone types an answer.
`name = input("Name? ")` waits for a name.
It waits for you to ____ a guess.
It waits for you to type a guess. Pick that, Run, and type a number in the output panel.

steps.instruction: "Nope!" isn't much help. Add hints: if the guess is too small, print `Higher!`; if it's too big, print `Lower!`. Use `elif guess < secret:` between the `if` and the `else`.
hints: Change the part after `if guess == secret:`.
`elif` adds another check. Python runs the first one that's True.
`if temp > 35:` … `elif temp > 20:` … `else:` …
`elif guess < secret:` then `    print("Higher!")`, then `else:` then `    print("______!")`.
Replace the else part with: `elif guess < secret:` / `    print("Higher!")` / `else:` / `    print("Lower!")`.

milestones.title: Keep guessing
milestones.goal: A full game that counts your tries.

steps.instruction: One guess isn't a game. A **while loop** keeps asking. Fill the blank so it keeps going *while the guess is not the secret*.

check.description: A real game! It keeps going until you win.

hints: The blank is in `while guess ___ secret:`.
The loop should repeat as long as the guess is wrong.
`==` means equal. `!=` means not equal.
`while guess _= secret:`
`while guess != secret:`. Run it and play!

steps.instruction: Keep score! Add `tries = 0` before the loop, `tries = tries + 1` inside it, and print how many tries it took at the end.

check.description: Now you can beat your best score!

hints: Three changes: one line above `while`, one inside the loop, and the last print.
A counter starts at 0 and goes up by 1 each time something happens.
`claps = 0`, then inside a loop `claps = claps + 1`, then `print(claps)`.
Before the loop: `tries = 0`. Inside: `    tries = tries + __`. At the end: `print("You got it in", tries, "tries!")`.
Add `tries = 0` above the while line, `    tries = tries + 1` under the input line, and change the last line to `print("You got it in", tries, "tries!")`.

milestones.title: The computer guesses
milestones.goal: A guessing machine that finds your number in 7 tries or fewer.

steps.instruction: Now the computer guesses **your** number! `(low + high) // 2` finds the middle. If your number is 70, what's its first guess?
steps.explain: (1 + 100) // 2 is 50: right in the middle. `//` divides and drops the leftover. Each answer cuts the possible numbers in half, so it never needs more than 7 tries for 1 to 100.
hints: Look at `guess = (low + high) // 2`. What are low and high at the start?
low is 1 and high is 100. `//` divides and throws away any leftover.
50. Pick it, then Run and answer higher, lower or yes.

steps.instruction: Play it! Think of a number and answer honestly. Can it always find it in **7 tries or fewer**? Then make it yours: change its messages, or make it 1 to 1000. Finish a game by typing **yes**.
hints: Play a full game first, answering higher, lower or yes.
To change the range, change `high = 100`. The messages are inside the `print(...)` lines.
`high = 1000` makes it 1 to 1000. It needs 10 tries at most.
Change a message, like `print("Hmm… is it", guess, "?")`.
Change `high = 100` to `high = 1000` and the first message to say 1 to 1000. Run it and type yes when it gets your number.
